title: The Tony Awards Air Tomorrow Night. For the First Time, an Indian-American Is Producing the Show.
excerpt: Raj Kapoor will produce the 79th Tony Awards at Radio City Music Hall, hosted by P!nk. Schmigadoon! and The Lost Boys lead with 12 nominations each.
body:
The 79th Tony Awards will be broadcast live from Radio City Music Hall on Sunday, June 7, at 8 PM ET on CBS and Paramount+. Pop icon P!nk will host. The front-runners are Schmigadoon! and The Lost Boys, tied at 12 nominations each. And for the first time in the ceremony's 79-year history, an Indian-American is producing Broadway's biggest night.

Raj Kapoor — not to be confused with the legendary Bollywood actor — is an Emmy-nominated television producer who has been named co-producer alongside Sarah Levine Hall and Jack Sussman. The trio takes over from White Cherry Entertainment, which had produced the ceremony since 2004. Kapoor's appointment marks a quiet but significant milestone for South Asian representation in the upper echelons of American entertainment infrastructure. Producers shape what audiences see, hear, and feel during the broadcast — they are the architects of the evening.

## What Is at Stake on Stage

The Tony nominations this year reflect a Broadway season that has swung between the adventurous and the nostalgic. Schmigadoon!, adapted from the beloved Apple TV+ series, is the cult-favourite-turned-Broadway-hit that has earned nominations across acting, direction, design, and score. The Lost Boys, matching it nomination for nomination, represents a different kind of theatrical ambition. Both are competing for Best Musical, the evening's marquee prize.

Other nominated productions include Chess, the Tim Rice and ABBA musical with a new book by Danny Strong; Oedipus, an innovative revival; and Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York), a musical featuring Christiani Pitts and Sam Tutty in leading roles.

The acting categories are stacked. Sara Chase is nominated for Best Leading Actress in a Musical for Schmigadoon!, while Ana Gasteyer is up for Best Featured Actress in a Musical from the same production.

## Broadway's Quiet Diversity Revolution

The Tony Awards have been on a slow but meaningful journey toward broader representation. In recent years, Asian American performers have made history at the ceremony — Nicole Scherzinger, Daniel Dae Kim, and Francis Jue were all nominated in the same year for the first time. Ruthie Ann Miles became the first Asian actor to win Best Featured Actress in a Musical in 2015.

But representation behind the camera — in producing, directing, and showrunning — has lagged. Kapoor's role as a producer of the Tony Awards broadcast puts a South Asian creative in a position that directly shapes the cultural conversation around Broadway. It is the kind of structural access that matters more than any single on-stage moment.

## What the Diaspora Should Know

For NRIs who grew up watching Bollywood award shows and now live in cities with thriving theatre scenes — New York, London, Toronto, Chicago — the Tonys are a natural bridge. Broadway has increasingly drawn from global stories and global talent. The current season includes productions that deal with identity, displacement, and the tension between tradition and reinvention — themes that resonate deeply with diaspora audiences.

The broadcast begins at 8 PM ET / 5 PM PT on Sunday. CBS will carry it live, with streaming on Paramount+. A pre-show, The Tony Awards: Act One, will air on CBS and Pluto TV before the main ceremony.

For those keeping track: 857 designated voters will decide the winners across 26 competitive categories. The season that is being honoured ran from April 28, 2025 to April 26, 2026. And the man making sure the cameras capture it all has a name that, in a different context and a different industry, would need no introduction at all.
author: Diaspora Desk
